To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high relapse after melarsoprl treatment observed in the Democratic Republic Congo sleeping sickness focus of Mbuji-May is associated with mutations in the aquaporin genes of the local T. brucei gambiens strains.
mutations in the Aqp2/3 locus may explain the high relapse of patients treated with melasoprol in the Mbuju-Mayi focus of the DRC.

the reduced in vitro melarsoprol susceptibility of T.b. gambiese strains isolated from patients that relapsed after melansoprol treatment is not caused by mutations in TbA1 but by mutations in the TbAQ2/3 locus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs and new drug targets for the chemotherapy of sleeping sickness.
the mechanisms underlying drug resistance in T.b. gambiese and may help to improve the treatment of sleeping sickness.
the identification of molecular mechanisms of melarsoprol resistance that can be exploited to develop new drugs for the treatment of African trypanosomiasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AQP2/2-3 locus is not a good marker for melarsoprol resistance.
the high melarspolor relapse rate in the Mbuju-Mayi focus is not due to mutations in TbAt1 but rather to mutations in the Aqp2/3 genes.
a combination of several factors may explain the high relapse in Mbuji Mayi, but that mutations in the Aqp locus is a likely contributing factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutations in AQP2/ AQP3 locus of T.b. gambiesne strains may be responsible for the reduced melarsoprl sensitivity and high melarsoprl relapse rates in some sleeping sickness foci.
mutations in AQP2/2/3 are associated with reduced melarsoplor sensitivity and that this may explain the high relapse in Mbuji Mayi.
the AQP2/2-3 locus is a potential target for drug discovery and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the AQP2/ AQP3 locus as a molecular marker for melarsoprol resistance may help in the selection of the best treatment for sleeping sickness patients in different sleeping sickness foci.
the TbAT1 gene does not appear to be involved in melarsoprol resistance of T.b. gambiensis strains from the DRC.
the AQP2 and AQP3 genes are important targets for the development of new anti-trypanosome drugs.
